New Novitec N-Largo Ferrari 12Cilindri Is THE Exotic Grand Tourer To Crave
21 photos
Photo: Novitec
With the 12Cilindri being Ferrari’s modern entry in the front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive stable, it is no wonder that certain tuners have launched all kinds of upgrades for this model ever since it became available some two years ago.
Novitec’s name is definitely on the list, as it has already introduced a few takes on this model. Fast forward to this week, though, and the renowned tuner now has the so-called N-Largo bundle available. Created in partnership with German designer Vittorio Strosek, just like other N-Largo projects introduced over the years, the extras are all about aerodynamic function, in addition to the enhanced design, and they definitely help the model stand out from the crowd much easier.
Well, assuming that you know your Ferrari 12Cilindris , that is, because the upgrades will definitely fly under the radar for the average Joe. But then again, this is what Novitec is famously known for, and that’s crafting all kinds of fine projects that do not go anywhere near the brash realm. And that’s why we (or I, in this case) adore their builds, because Novitec can easily host a tuning course for other tuners. And it’s been extremely hard not to mention Mansory’s name here. Wait a minute...
The N-Largo version of the Ferrari 12Cilindri benefits from larger wheel arches at the front and rear. The fender flares have made the supercar (it’s actually an exotic GT, as mentioned above) much wider than before. According to Novitec, the modded 12Cilindri in question is (almost) 3 inches (7 cm) wider at the front and 5 inches (13 cm) wider at the rear.
Photo: Novitec Rocker panels between the wide fenders are also on deck, and they make the car more aerodynamic. The carbon covers for the door mirrors contribute to the racy look of the car . There are also large air intakes at the front, an integrated spoiler that reduces the nose-lift at high speeds, and a new hood with integrated and carbon-framed air outlets that provide a view of the two red intake manifolds of the V12, which also optimizes the engine bay’s heat dissipation.
Additional upgrades include the ducktail spoiler at the rear, with its three-piece design, which has been integrated into the N-Largo widebody kit. A dry carbon diffuser can also be seen at the rear, as well as two dual tailpipe tips at the left and right, which are part of the tuner’s sports exhaust system. This component features butterfly valves, and Novitec also offers a version with 999 fine-gold plating for a more exclusive look, which also improves the heat dissipation. The sports catalysts are optional.
The special makeover does not end here, because the Ferrari 12Cilindri N-Largo by Novitec also benefits from new wheels. Made in partnership with Vossen, they are called the Novitec NF12 N-Largo, and they measure 12x22 inches at the rear and 10x21 inches at the front, wrapped in 325/30 and 275/35 tires respectively. Courtesy of the Novitec sports springs, the vehicle rides roughly inches (30 mm) closer to the ground.
Now, the new exhaust system likely allows the engine to produce a bit more oomph, but since the upgrade is not significant at all, Novitec hasn’t mentioned the revised output and thrust. But even without any outside intervention, the mill, which is a naturally aspirated V12, in case you forgot, with a 6.5-liter displacement, is very potent.
Photo: Novitec The output is 818 hp (830 ps/610 kW ) and the thrust stands at 500 pound-feet (678 Nm) of torque, as per the model’s official spec sheet. This allows the Ferrari 12Cilindri to reach 62 mph (100 kph) in just 2.9 seconds, and flat-out, it will do up to 211 mph (340 kph) wherever the road and legislation allow it.
Novitec offers the N-Largo Ferrari 12Cilindri as a complete package, including the supercar, but alternatively, it will also convert vehicles to this configuration upon request. Therefore, interested parties must reach out to them to discuss the details, including the finances, because the money haven’t been mentioned in the press release. And if you find out how much it costs, then feel free to drop a line below and share this information with us.
In the meantime, we will remind you that Ferrari’s 12Cilindri hit the assembly line at Maranello, Italy, in 2024. It is the successor to the 812 Superfast, which replaced the F12berlinetta in the Prancing Horse’s stable, and the latter succeeded the 599. It is 186.2 inches (4,730 mm) long, 85.7 inches (2,176 mm) wide, and 50.8 inches (1,290 mm) tall. The wheelbase measures 106.3 inches (2,700 mm), and the car has a curb weight of over 3,400 pounds (1,560 kg).
Two body styles are available, a two-door berlinetta (coupe) and a two-door retractable hardtop convertible, and both feature the same front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive layout, and pack the same old-school naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 engine, mated to an eight-speed DCT , in the same configuration.

New G65 BMW X5 Gets Visited by the Tuning Fairy, Is This a Good Look for the Neue Klasse Model?
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | waido.kits
The paint has barely dried on the body of the new-generation BMW X5 , but the model has already been visited by the tuning fairy. And no, it’s not a CGI-infused makeover this time around, as you too could make your very own example look exactly like this.
Signed by @waido.kits and shared on social media a few days ago, this is the final design of their body kit, which includes the usual add-ons on the outside. It is offered as a bundle, though interested parties can also order some of these parts individually. And if you must know, the company is already accepting pre-orders.
The makeover certainly makes the G65 BMW X5 a lot more visible. Not that it flies under the radar, as the Neue Klasse look has created what is arguably the most controversial X5 ever. Therefore, a few aftermarket tweaks could be just what the doctor ordered in order to make the entire thing more appealing from a visual perspective. However, the pictured example hasn’t been “tweaked,” but modified to the point where it looks a lot more aggressive.
Actually, “pictured” may not be the best word to describe it, because “rendered” would suit it much better. That’s because the makeover may be real, and available for pre-order as we speak, as mentioned above, but the car in question does not exist outside Fantasy Land. Nevertheless, it does reveal what your tuned X5 from the new generation could look for, if you settle for these upgrades, in these color combinations.
Photo: Instagram | waido.kits So, what is new, you ask? Well, the hood for one, which features some extra bulges on it. The add-ons on the sides of the front bumper have also come from the aftermarket world, and so has the new splitter, which looks very sporty. The grille appears to have been tweaked as well, and the changes do not end here.
Far from it, actually, because this new-gen BMW X5 also benefits from fender flares. The wheel arch attachments have made it a lot wider than before, and we can also see that there are new side skirt add-ons on deck, too, as part of the visual makeover, as well as panels on the lower parts of the doors, right above the side skirts.
At the rear, this machine sports a new diffuser, as well as some extras on the sides of the bumper, as well as what seems to be a new roof-mounted spoiler. The lighting units on the outside have been tinted, and so have the windows. Some of the new components are presented in glossy black, others have been virtually painted in the same color as the rest of the body, whereas some have a forged carbon look.
These include the wheel arch attachments and the hood, and due to these, the BMW X5 in question sends some Mansory vibes. In my opinion, anyway. The premium mid-size crossover also sits a lot closer to the ground, so the suspension has been altered, at least in these digital illustrations. The wheels are new, have a concave design, and are a two-tone proposal.
Photo: Instagram | waido.kits Waido’s name decorates the tailgate in the renderings shared in our gallery, and the tuner says that the extras mentioned above can be equipped to all G65s, as well as they feature the M Package . And just so you know, in addition to carbon fiber, which is a must-have when it comes to high-end modern-day tuning jobs, some of the add-ons have been made of ABS plastic.
A power boost is not part of the makeover, so we will remind you that the 40 and 40 xDrive versions of the Neue Klasse BMW X5 are offered with a 3.0-liter TwinPower Turbo engine. The straight-six mill produces 394 hp (294 kW/400 ps), enabling 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in 5.2 and 5.1 seconds, respectively.
The plug-in hybrid model , which is known as the X5 50E xDrive, is faster. It deals with the 0-60 mph sprint in 4.6 seconds, aided by the 483 horsepower (360 kW/490 ps) produced in total by the electrified inline-six. It is just as punchy and fast as its predecessor, though it can now travel up to 44 miles (71 km) on zero emissions instead of 39 miles (63 km).
Pricing for the 2027 BMW X5 starts at $69,800 for the base 40 model in the States, and the 40 xDrive is available from $72,100. As for the PHEV, you are looking at a minimum of $77,500, excluding destination, options, and dealer fees.
Waido hasn’t said anything about the pricing part when it comes to its tuning bundle for the G65 BMW X5 , though it invites interested parties to reach out to them in order to discuss the details. Does this look suit the new X5? Drop a line below and tell us all about it. EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
The Virtual Ford Mustang GTD Competition Gets Unmasked and Looks Ready to Hit the Green Hell Again
12 photos
Photo: avarvarii / Instagram
The Ford Motor Company has been pretty busy as of late – launching through its Ford Custom Garage program the fresh 300-horsepower Maverick SV300T Black and Bronze Packages or through Ford Racing Parts a Predator supercharged V8 crate engine pack and an accompanying Tremec dual-clutch transmission pegged for delivery starting with the first quarter of 2027.
The only annoying thing about the Blue Oval is that in America it has just one passenger car on sale – the S650 iteration of the iconic Ford Mustang. It’s available as a coupe or convertible with the EcoBoost inline-four turbo or the Coyote V8 and the Predator V8 in various configurations, at least. But it can’t compete with the Dodge Charger, which is also available as a sedan, for example, because the rumors about a proper four-door Mustang (not the high-riding Mach-E) have not panned out just yet.
Instead, Ford is busy making the regular Mustang as enticing as possible – they recently added the Dark Horse SC version with a 795-hp version of the Predator V8 , which is also used in an 815-hp form in the Mustang GTD supercar. The Dark Horse SC was also made available as a Convertible recently, as the next summer season is drawing nearer and nearer.
But the rumor mill is also relentless – and it recently found out that Ford might be thinking about bringing back the iconic Cobra moniker. That’s a great idea, since the Shelby GT500 is now a Dark Horse SC; the reports peg a follow-up of the Shelby GT350 and GT350R in the form of revived Cobra and Cobra R models.
Alas, we haven’t gathered here across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI alongside a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators for that snake. Instead, Andrei Avarvarii, the virtual artist behind Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (also known as ' avarvarii ' on social media), has taken a thorough, in-depth CGI look at Ford's upcoming plans and came up with this – the series production Ford Mustang GTD Competition.
It’s not a surprising model – the upgraded street-legal performance variant of the standard Mustang GTD was used earlier this year during the spring testing season to snatch back the American Nürburgring Nordschleife record from the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X by Dirk Muller, posting a new US record time of 6:40.835. In fact, it seems the GTC Competition model is so good that one of Ford’s engineers also ran a separate hot lap of 6:49.337!
Now, the pixel master has decided to unmask the Ford Mustang GTD Competition that will probably cost even more than the regular GTD when it launches sometime before the end of the year or early in 2027. The CGI expert wanted us to see the new version in its most ‘natural environment,’ so they showed us the renderings in a fancy crimson shade with white racing stripes in a sterile studio setting, then brought the Ford out onto a racetrack in white with blue stripes, in blue, and also in yellow with blue stripes. EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Previews the Future of the Tenere Adventure Bikes With Mysterious 4 Concept
Time Capsule 1962 Ford Thunderbird Ragtop Rocks Rare Factory Option, Original V8 Is Even Rarer
30 photos
Photo: Exotic Car Trader
Ford and Chevrolet have been taking turns and punches at one another ever since the Bowtie came into being. There hasn’t been a single automobile type in the world that the two companies wouldn’t build either to one-up the rival, or to retaliate to an initiative of said adversary. However, Chevrolet had the last word when it came to sportscars – the Corvette is still America’s Sportscar, no matter what Ford did, does, or will do. That didn’t mean the Blue Oval didn’t have a go at the genre.
The 1955 Ford Thunderbird was the two-seater that was definitely NOT a sportscar, but outsold the Corvette so dramatically, it nearly drove it into the ground. Nearly. The ‘Vette sold 700 cars in ’55, while the all-new “personal luxury automobile” from FoMoCo dispatched 16,155 units. Chevrolet must have had nerves of steel, seeing how for each of its Corvettes , Ford made 23 Thunderbirds.
Then along came 1958, when Detroit underwent a massive change in styling across the board, and Ford decided two-seaters were a thing of the past already, and simply stretched the luxury ‘Bird into a four-passenger two-door vehicle. It wasn’t exotic anymore, but it was profitable. Sales went through the roof – 37,892 cars – and Henry Ford II never looked back. He did have some second thoughts, though. Remember the Sports Roadster? Here’s one to refresh your memory.
Not only is it a rare Ford Thunderbird, it’s also very much Rangoon Red. This 1962 T-bird Sports Roadster rocks some extra rare goodies upfront. Showing 30,398 miles, it pairs a matching red cabin with a white power soft top and its removable body-color fiberglass tonneau cover. Coincidentally, the 1962 brochure presented the all-new body style in the exact same color.
Photo: Exotic Car Trader What separates this drop-top from ordinary Thunderbirds sits directly in front and behind the driver. Let’s go front to back: underhood sits Ford's rare M-code 390-cubic-inch V8 topped with three Holley two-barrel carburetors. Rated at 340 horsepower and 430 lb-ft of torque (345 PS, 583 Nm) with 10.5:1 compression, it pairs with a 3-speed Cruise-O-Matic automatic and dual exhaust.
Equipment spans chrome wire wheels, Swing-Away steering, power windows, a power driver's seat, and an AM radio, though M-code hardware precluded factory air conditioning. And, let’s be honest, when you get a ragtop, you don’t plan to make it a winter beater. Whoever ordered the Thunderbird didn’t buy it as their first and only car.
Back in 1962, ordering a Thunderbird to this exact specification required deep pockets. The Sports Roadster carried a base price of $5,439—roughly $651 above the $4,788 standard convertible—already bundling Cruise-O-Matic, power steering, power brakes, the tonneau cover, and wire wheels.
Photo: Exotic Car Trader Adding the $242 M-code engine, $113 push-button AM radio, $106 power windows, $92 four-way power driver's seat, and $25 Swing-Away steering wheel brought the tally to $6,017, or $6,059 with $42 whitewall tires, before destination charges. That was Cadillac money right there.
The Sports Roadster moniker was born from nostalgia and clever corporate improvisation. After Ford expanded the Thunderbird into a four-passenger cruiser for 1958, sales surged, yet purists kept demanding a two-seat successor. Ford Division chief Lee Iacocca tasked designer Bud Kaufman with a practical solution. Kaufman crafted a removable fiberglass tonneau cover with twin headrest fairings hiding the rear bench, paired with a passenger grab bar and unique fender emblems.
Ford built the Sports Roadster for just two model years, 1962 and 1963, equipping every example exclusively with the 3-speed Cruise-O-Matic automatic. Buyers chose between the standard 300-horsepower four-barrel Z-code 390-cubic-inch V8 and the optional 340-horsepower Tri-Power M-code 390. The engine was added to the roster in January 1962, and Ford quietly dropped it midway through 1963.
Photo: Exotic Car Trader Standard 48-spoke Kelsey-Hayes wire wheels completed the look, though early versions needed an urgent factory fix after one collapsed under Elvis Presley.
Production stayed remarkably tight across that 24-month window, totaling just 1,882 Sports Roadsters. Output reached its high point in 1962 with 1,427 cars, split between 1,307 Z-code four-barrel models and just 120 examples fitted with the triple-carburetor M-code V8. Interest cooled sharply in 1963 as production tumbled to 455 units, comprising 418 Z-code cars and a microscopic 37 M-code Roadsters.
All told, Ford built 1,725 Z-code and only 157 M-code Sports Roadsters across both model years. as for M-code T-birds in total, the 1962 model year saw just 25 hardtops ordered with the six-barrel powerhouse, putting the grand total to 145 personal luxury Fords powered by the muscular motor.
Those scarce roadsters belonged to the third-generation Thunderbird, nicknamed the "Bullet Bird" and built from 1961 through 1963. Styled with sleek jet-age lines by Bill Boyer, it gained instant prestige pacing the 1961 Indianapolis 500 and joining President John F. Kennedy's inaugural parade. Across three model years, Dearborn built 214,375 third-generation Thunderbirds : 73,051 in 1961, peaking at 78,011 in 1962, and finishing with 63,313 in 1963.
Photo: Exotic Car Trader Breaking down the 1962 peak by body style illustrates just how heavily buyers favored closed-roof comfort. Out of 78,011 Thunderbirds built that year, hardtop coupes accounted for 68,127 units—a combined figure that absorbed the newly launched vinyl-roofed Landau, estimated at roughly 15% of hardtop production.
Open-air variants represented a distant minority, with 8,457 standard convertibles and 1,427 Sports Roadsters leaving the Wixom, Michigan plant, putting Sports Roadsters at under 2% of total 1962 output.
Rarity alone , however, has not immunized the Sports Roadster from collector-market gravity over the past 5 years. Following a broader cooling period that saw Sports Roadster values dip 23% late in 2023, standard Z-code 1962 examples have traded within an accessible band. Verified sales routinely landed between $26,400 and $70,000, highlighted by $44,000 at Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale in 2024, $49,500 at Mecum Glendale in 2026, and $70,000 on Bring a Trailer in February 2026.
Photo: Exotic Car Trader Even factory M-code 1962 Sports Roadsters have swung wildly over the past 5 years. Verified sales span $42,900 in 2026 and $48,160 in 2025 to $77,000 in both 2022 and 2025, while premier cars reached $140,000 at Broad Arrow Amelia in 2026 and $165,000 in 2022. The all-time record for any Sports Roadster stands at $220,000, achieved in 2023 at Mecum by a 1962 M-code example.
This specific car seen in the video attached below also carries notable provenance , having previously resided in John Staluppi's Cars of Dreams Collection. When Staluppi auctioned part of his museum at Barrett-Jackson Palm Beach in April 2018, this Rangoon Red Thunderbird sold for $85,800 ($78k hammer price). Less than a year later, it returned to Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale in January 2019, and hammered for $145,000, nearly double than eight months before.
Measured against broader market medians, the current asking price of $161,299 set by the seller on the Exotic Car Trader platform is still a long way from the top. But it’s also a long way from buyers’ expectations – the current high bid is a reality-checking $12,000, with three days to go.

source_document.body:
EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
Upcoming Fiat Koala, the Italian Citroen 2CV, Also Gains a Hybrid Version Across Imagination Land
8 photos
Photo: kdesignag / Instagram
Back at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, the massive Stellantis group decided to rule the event in Paris with over 60 brand-new vehicles – nine of them being concept cars.
There was even a ‘The Night Before’ event just like in the good old days of major automotive shows with plenty of reveals – Alfa Romeo, Citroen, DS Automobiles, Fiat, Opel, and Peugeot presented six of the most important prototypes: Cuorerosso, 2 CV Concept, DS F3VER, Multiplay , STX Concept, and the RCZ Vision.
Of them all, the rumor mill is pretty sure that the Citroen 2CV will enter series production, with Stellantis looking to revive the spirit of the legendary original but with modern traits: fully electric, made in Europe, and accessible at a starting price of €15k. The accompanying concept was more than fancy, but most likely the real Citroen will be a bit more serious – the French automaker already has experience with the barren Ami quadricycle.
But, as it turns out, the new Citroen 2CV won’t come alone to make sure it becomes even less expensive to produce – Fiat’s next European city car got a fresh name and slated production in Italy alongside the French version. Called Fiat Koala, the new city EV was actually expected to arrive at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, but instead Fiat graced us with the Multiplay, a concept hinting at a potential successor for the rather unpopular Multipla compact minivan.
Set to arrive in 2027, the upcoming Fiat Koala was only revealed by name by Arnauld Belloni, Fiat's new CEO, during an interview at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, and obviously nobody knows its exact looks. No worries, as the rumor mill has quickly joined the chat and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators have stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to lend a helping hand.
For example, Kleber Silva, a Brazil-based virtual artist known as " KDesign AG " on social media, has decided to have a CGI go at imagining the next small Fiat and created their vision of the Koala for their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project. Based on the new Stellantis E-Car platform, the Fiat Koala will be one of the group’s upcoming electric city cars targeting a new category by the European Union promoting small and affordable EVs – kind of like the Japanese kei cars but with batteries only.
Anyway, the pixel master not only imagined the design of the new model but also took things a step forward, envisioning the potentially even more affordable Fiat Koala Hybrid version. It has a funky design with retro elements like the square headlights plus taillights and the third color mixed with the main orange-and-black dual-tone attire, plus an upright stance to allow enough space for all four people. EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Previews the Future of the Tenere Adventure Bikes With Mysterious 4 Concept
Ford Oakville Assembly Returns to Vehicle Production With F-Series Super Duty Line
10 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford's very first Oakville-produced Super Duties are now heading to dealers, giving the Detroit-based automaker a third North American assembly plant for its biggest F-Series models. Oakville Assembly received in the ballpark of CAD 5 billion to get here, and there is a lot more going on here that meets the eye.
Beyond the substantial reconstruction, the Canadian vehicle production complex had to bring together a workforce that spent years building very different vehicles. In the first instance, Oakville specialized in a wide range of Fords , Mercurys, and Edsels.
Then came the pickup truck and commercial vehicle era, which lasted from the 1960s all the way to 2004. From the 1990s to 2007, said complex also built the Windstar, Freestar, and Monterey people carriers.
The wagon and crossover era started in the latter part of the 2000s, with nameplates including the Lincoln MKX, Ford Edge, Flex, MKT, and Nautilus. Edge production ended in May 2024, when the Oakville complex was idled in preparation for an electric vehicle pivot. That plan fell apart, with FoMoCo deciding on F-Series Super Duty workhorses instead.
Dearborn confirmed the switchover in July 2024. The media release published back then clearly states "future multi-energy technology" for the next generation of the Super Duty line, which is another way of saying that hybrid trucks or greater levels of electrification are on the menu. Whether that means an extended-range electric Super Duty is planned as well, we can't say for certain yet.
Photo: Ford Spreading F-Series Super Duty production across three sites will help North American dealers accommodate more configurations while shortening customer waiting times, particularly for commercial buyers.
A contractor, a utility company, or an ambulance operator might need particular configurations rather than whichever truck happens to sit on a dealership lot, and those customers represent an important part of the Super Duty business in both the US and the Canadian market.
In preparation for Super Duty production, FoMoCo rebuilt the final assembly areas, paint operations, and body shops in just around two years. The American automaker has also added its first stamping facility in Canada. Helped by collaborative products, assembly line workers do their thing on a line that stretches approximately 1,000 feet (a little over 300 meters).
AI-enabled cameras inspect the pickups as they move through Oakville Assembly, giving workers another way to identify potential quality concerns rather than relying exclusively on end-of-line inspections. As of November 2026, the facility is home to more than 2,000 employees. The mix between production and skilled trades hasn't been detailed by the Dearborn-based automaker.
Skilled trades in this context stands for everything from electricians to millwrights, toolmakers, and robotics specialists. Think of them as the guys and gals who keep things operational. Production workers, meanwhile, handle assembly. Oakville Assembly received approval to ship its first Super Duty trucks two weeks ahead of schedule, and Ford claims the quality at Oakville matches that of Kentucky.
Encouraging launch results, for sure, but sustained production and the NHTSA 's recall database will provide a much better indication of how consistently the new operation performs. In the first instance, Oakville Assembly promises up to 100,000 additional units of Super Duty production capacity per year.

1969 Dodge Super Bee A12 Joins MCACN With 2,700 Original Miles, Stunning Survivor
13 photos
Photo: Geoff Stunkard's Zookeeper's Diary/YouTube
It's that time of the year, folks! This year's Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals (MCACN) is opening its doors to the public today, meaning we'll see some of America's greatest classic muscle cars under the same roof. And we're kicking off the coverage with a very special 1969 Dodge Super Bee .
Filmed while it was being judged for MCACN's already iconic Concours section, this 1969 Super Bee is not your average affordable Mopar, which was built in 27,800 examples that year. It's an A12 version, meaning that it packs the iconic 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) RB V8 with the six-barrel carburetor setup.
The Six-Pack mill was brand new in 1969 and quite exclusive. Before it found its way in all B-body Mopars in 1970, the six-barrel 440 was only available in two nameplates in 1969: the Dodge Super Bee and the Plymouth Road Runner. It wasn't a stand-alone option either but was part of the A12 package.
In addition to the engine, the bundle included a lift-off fiberglass hood (in matte black), 15x6 black steel wheels wrapped in performance tires, heavy-duty brakes, a Dana 60 Sure-Grip rear axle with a 4.10 ratio, and heavy-duty suspension with Hemi-spec leaf springs (S15 Police Handling Package). The A12 badge basically turned the Super Bee into a factory drag car.
The Six-Pack mill, by the way, came with 390 horsepower and 490 pound-feet of torque. The latter figure was identical to the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi (which delivered 425 horsepower).
The Super Bee A12 is also special when it comes to production numbers. That's because Dodge sold only 1,907 units, meaning a production ratio of only 6.9%. The number splits between 420 coupes and 1,487 hardtops. As far as transmissions go, 814 were ordered with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic, while 1,093 got the four-speed manual.
Seeing a 1969 Super Bee A12 in such fantastic condition is a rare event, but this Mopar has a massive feat to brag about. Although it may seem to be a finely restored example, this Super Bee is actually an unrestored survivor . It has only 2,700 miles (4,345 km) on the odometer, as it spent most of its life in storage. It was pampered since new and soldiered on as a 100% original time capsule.
The story goes that the original owner drove the car rarely until 1973. That year, the Super Bee was parked never to be seen again for decades. The car changed hands when the original owner passed away, being purchased by his best friend. The fellow who brought it to MCACN this year is the third owner.
One of 267 hardtop models fitted with the TorqueFlite automatic gearbox, this blue-on-blue Super Bee A12 is still finished in the factory, which looks flawless even upon close inspection. The original window sticker reveals that it's also a well-equipped model.
In addition to the A12 package and the mandatory options (wheels/tires and suspension), it was also ordered with the tinted windshield, three-speed wipers, fender-mounted turn signals, tachometer, power steering, sports steering wheel, and a black vinyl roof.
The same document also reveals the healthy premium the A12 package added to a Super Bee in 1969. The drivetrain and the suspension cost $491.5, which accounted for over 12% of the vehicle's total price. With the destination charge included, this Mopar set the owner back over $4,000.
There's no info on how many points this car was awarded by the MCACN judging panel , but we're probably looking at one of the finest survivors out there. Hit the play button below to check it out.

This Is the Ford That Inspired Jason's First Car in GTA 6: Meet the Vapid Ganado
14 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
The Vapid Ganado is the car on everybody’s lips these days, and it’s not even a real model. The GTA 6 craze has reached the level where people are searching the web for ways to buy a Ganado, and to everyone’s surprise, this is a car that you can actually buy and drive.
Well, sort of, as nobody has ever created a Vapid Ganado as you know it from the new Grand Theft Auto . But the Ganado is based on a vehicle that actually existed, and if money isn’t an issue, you should be able to find out in good shape online.
The Ganado is the first car you get in GTA 6. It’s not the most eye-candy truck, but on the other hand, it serves its purpose quite right. Considering it’s a pickup, you use it to carry stuff around, such as Lucia’s clothes when she gets out of prison, groceries, your loadout, and so on.
This is precisely how the model that the Ganado is based on was born.
Photo: Ford Enter the Ford Ranchero.
The Ranchero came to be in 1957 when Ford was still the number one carmaker in the United States. Things were about to change in 1958, when Chevrolet secured the leading spot, but the introduction of the Ranchero made perfect sense for people who wanted a good-looking car with a utilitarian upgrade.
Based on Ford’s full-size platform, the Ranchero sported the front of full-size cars mixed with a pickup-like bed in the back. It was powered by the same engines as its full-size siblings, beginning with a 223 six and ending with the 292 and the 352 V8s.
The Ranchero was so popular that Chevrolet had no other option but to come up with a model of its own specifically to compete with it. The El Camino was based on the same approach, with the full-size platform spearheaded by the Impala serving as the development platform.
However, the El Camino wasn’t as popular as the Ranchero, and it was pulled after only two years. It was reintroduced in 1964 as part of Chevrolet’s existing lineups.
The Ranchero survived and continued to command a significant customer share.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The Ranchero lineup was expanded in 1970, when Ford added the Squire - a more luxurious version of the pickup truck - and the GT - whose main focus was the performance under the hood. Each model came with unique features and more or less powerful engines, depending on the audience they were going after.
For example, the GT could be ordered with a 429 Cobra Jet with a shaker hood air scoop, Ram Air induction, and the performance handling package. The top configuration produced no more, no less than 370 horsepower.
Ford did not want the Ranchero to lose its utilitarian purpose despite going for more powerful and more luxurious options.
The base version was still fitted with a 200 ci six-cylinder engine that developed only 155 horsepower. This engine made sense for people who wanted the Ranchero for actual work.
The V8 offering started with a 302 rated at 220 horsepower and continued with a 351 that could be had with a two-barrel or a four-barrel carburetor. These engines produced 250 and 300 horsepower, respectively.
The 429 was available in two configurations: the Thunder Jet with 360 horsepower and the Cobra with 370 horsepower.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Theoretically, the Ganado is offered with a 434 engine, as indicated by the tags on the side of the truck. You can see these tags in the photos I took with the Ganado in its standard configuration. The yellow paint is the one I applied for free, though Ultimate buyers can also customize the vehicle with the Retro Build for free.
Obviously, you can customize the Ganado even further as you play the game, as there are lots of options, beginning with the engine under the hood and ending with the wheels and other cosmetic improvements. They all cost serious dollars, so you’ll have to work quite a lot for Brian to be able to afford all of these.
However, the Ganado is proving to be quite an efficient ride for Jason, especially in the first chapters in the game. It’ll end up coming in handy after Lucia is released from prison, too, but I’m with most players here - the more you play, the more tempted you are to purchase another car.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution So there you go, if you’re such a big fan of the Ganado, you can actually build one yourself if you get a 1970 Ranchero project car. These cars shouldn’t cost more than a couple of thousand dollars, considering they aren’t necessarily the most sought-after.
Of course, you won’t get a tip-top shape at this price, but a running engine and a bed that can still hold your stuff without falling through the rust holes should be doable at $2,000.

Mansory's New Mercedes-AMG G 63 Doesn't Only Look the Part, It Could Also Save Your Life
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa
Another week, another Mansory build . Only this time, the vehicle you see above is on the more special side of things, because the modifications haven’t only made it more visible in a sea of Mercedes-AMG G 63 premium trucks, as this thing has the ability to save your life.
What does this mean? That we are looking at a bulletproof ride. Images of this project were shared recently on Mansory’s social media channels by the tuner’s US arm, and guess what? The company has not revealed that many things about it. In fact, it hasn’t revealed anything, other than the fact that it is armored, adding that “security is important.” And it is, though if you are shopping for a bulletproof machine, then you may want to consider changing jobs.
The level of ballistic protection hasn’t been mentioned at all, though we can clearly see that this Mercedes-AMG G 63 features extra thick windows. And if it is anything like other similar armored cars that we have covered, then it should also benefit from armor plating within the doors. Chances are the entire passenger compartment has been completely sealed from the exterior, and if we were to guess, we’d say that it could survive multiple rounds and drive away, keeping its occupants safe.
High-end armored cars usually benefit from additional other things. An air filtration system is usually on deck, the engine, battery, and fuel tank are usually sealed, and armor plating is also found on its belly, so that it could survive light explosives being detonated underneath. Run-flat tires should also be a thing, and chances are it might also sport an intercom, as well as some strobe lights, in addition to other things.
Mind you, this is our (or my, in this case) two cents and should be taken with the proverbial pinch of salt for obvious reasons. The rest of the Mercedes-AMG G 63 in question does not look bad at all, though that is probably due to its glossy black exterior paint finish, because black tends to hide quirky designs perfectly. Nevertheless, this thing does not seem to be on the brash side of things at all. In fact, it is quite nice to look at, and proves that Mansory definitely knows how to create some cool projects.
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa The truck in question seems to be a bit wider than usual due to the fender flares and other components. It features new side steps that are illuminated, as well as a reworked bumper at the front that has plenty of extras. Speaking of extras, these also include the additional dual daytime running light strips on the outer edges of the bumper. The central air intake has also been modified, and we can also see that this ride has a new apron that is on the sportier side of things.
The main grille has been changed, and instead of the traditional Panamericana design with vertical slats of the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63 , it features a new pattern, and it is decorated with the tuner’s logo in the middle. The headlamp surrounds appear to have come from the aftermarket world as well, and the hood, with its vented and a lot more aggressive design, is also on the special side of things.
At the rear, Mansory has refrained itself from adding an extra pair of taillights, as it has done to other projects based on the popular German truck. However, the rear bumper is new, from what we can tell. It features some fake vent-like elements on each side of the license plate recess, as well as an integrated skirt on the lower part, and it has been extended toward the sides. The roof-mounted spoiler is also new, and so is the spare wheel holder that now displays the tuner’s name.
In addition to the glossy black finish, this Mercedes-AMG G 63 also features some forged carbon elements, though it’s not too brash, as we already told you. Due to the bulletproof makeover, it is likely that the suspension has been modified to cope with the extra weight. But then again, that’s our two cents. The wheels are familiar, as we have seen them on numerous Mansory projects, and they are definitely not bad at all, are they?
Photo: Instagram | mansory.usa For whatever reason, Mansory hasn’t provided a clear look inside this bulletproof G-Wagen, and that probably means that the interior hasn’t been touched with the tuning stick, with an obvious emphasis on the word “probably.” The pictures shared in the gallery show that the cockpit is dressed in black leather upholstery, and also features some metal trim, as well as the usual gear one would expect from such a thing.
Armored vehicles usually have a bit more oomph, and Mansory definitely has the ability to boost the output and thrust of the 4.0-liter bi-turbo V8 engine powering the Mercedes-AMG G 63, as most of its builds based on this model have more power. But is that the case here, too? Your guess is as good as ours, and since the tuner hasn’t revealed much about this ride, it is impossible to tell whether it is punchier or not.
Nonetheless, even with no outside intervention, the V8 engine is still capable of producing 577 hp (430 kW/585 ps) and 627 pound-feet (850 Nm) of torque. The peak thrust is available between 2,500 and 3,500 rpm, and the maximum output at 6,000 rpm. The stock AMG G 63 hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.3 seconds, though due to the added weight, this one should be a few seconds slower.
No details have been released when it comes to the availability part, so we do not know whether this ride is for sale, of it is being used by Mansory’s US division as a very cool marketing tool. Still, if you want one of these, then we’d advise you to reach out to the tuner and discuss the details. And before wrapping it up, let us know what you think about this armored Mercedes- AMG G 63 from Mansory. Is it a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mansory USA (@mansory.usa)

Small businesses shipping goods to overseas customers are the primary beneficiaries of a new AI-powered tool developed by DHL Express that simplifies product classification required on customs declarations and ensures descriptions are accurate.
The parcel and freight transportation company said last week that its smart identification capability is now available in the United States and a handful of other countries in the Americas.
The launch marks the first time AI-powered item identification has been integrated at scale into a live, customer-facing international express booking process, according to DHL Express.
Other freight management firms are also offering ways to ease customs compliance burdens for customers. Flexport, for example, this year added an AI classification tool to its customs software suite that generates a suggested tariff code. FedEx and UPS have digital trade tools designed to help customers review tariff code classifications and other document requirements, and accurately include duty calculations at checkout from online stores, but they don’t use AI to essentially replace a complex task the way DHL does with photo identification.
Every item in a package needs an adequate description on the customs form so customs authorities can assess duties, check compliance and clear goods. Shippers are required to state what the item is, what it is made of and its intended purpose.
Inaccurate or incomplete item descriptions are a common cause of customs delays and shipment holds. The new capability uses advanced computer vision to analyze a customer-generated photo of an item and instantly generate a structured, customs-compliant description, with the goal of improving data quality and reducing the potential for customs delays.
“For many businesses, one of the most challenging parts of international shipping is simply describing what they are sending to meet regulatory requirements,” said Greg Hewitt, CEO, DHL Express U.S., in a news release. “With AI-powered item identification, we’re taking the guesswork out of that process. Customers can simply take a photo and get a customs-compliant description in seconds, making it easier to get shipments right from the start and move them across borders with greater speed and confidence.”
The capability is particularly valuable for small and medium-sized enterprises , which represent approximately 86% of DHL Express customers in the U.S. Unlike larger companies that may have dedicated customs and trade compliance specialists, smaller businesses often have fewer resources to navigate complex international shipping requirements. As more SMEs explore international markets, the need for simple, intuitive tools to help them get shipments right from the start continues to grow. The number of small businesses in the U.S. using DHL Express for exports has increased 6% year over year, underscoring the opportunity to make international shipping more accessible.
The capability is particularly relevant as U.S. businesses expand trade with China, Hong Kong, Canada and Australia, and across growing sectors including e-commerce, manufacturing, automotive and fashion.
DHL said using the capability is simple. Customers photograph an item with a standard smartphone or connected device, and the AI system identifies the object and generates a structured description within seconds. Customers can review, edit or override the suggested description before submitting their shipment. No DHL Express account is required.
The U.S. is one of 10 markets in the Americas where the capability is now live, joining Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Mexico and Peru.
The launch is part of ongoing investments by DHL in digital technologies aimed at facilitating international shipping tasks. DHL said the new capability will be rolled out to more markets in 2027.
The DHL Group generated revenues of approximately 82.9 billion euros, equivalent to $91 billion in 2025. During the third quarter, DHL’s revenue increased 12.6% year over year to $25.4 billion.
